name: copy_field_and_clear_flag
description: Copies one byte from a source offset of the record to another offset and then zeroes a flag byte in the same record. It makes no calls and touches no hardware, and it returns straight to its caller.

name: advance_counter_and_reset_phase
description: Adds a per-record step byte to a counter byte and compares the result with the threshold in the low byte of the data register. Once the counter reaches the threshold it reloads it from a second record byte and clears a flag byte, otherwise it returns unchanged.

name: decode_channel_command_byte
description: Decodes a command byte for one of four per-channel state blocks, chosen from bits of the upper data register byte. Three reserved top values set flag bytes or clear a status byte, lower values store a value and a table-derived pointer, and the remaining values store a second parameter and reload a table entry.

name: dispatch_channel_command_record
description: Reads a signed command byte from an input record and branches on it. A minus ten copies two bytes and sets a flag, a minus eleven clears a flag, and the other values either store a table entry or save a parameter and reload a table entry, and the stack argument is written back to the input record before returning.

name: clear_flag_or_store_entry
description: Handles a signed command byte from an input record: a minus eleven clears a flag in the state record, values below 191 store lookup-table data and set a flag, and higher values store a second parameter and reload a table entry. The stack argument is written back to the input record before returning.

name: store_table_entry_from_record
description: Stores a lookup-table value and a table-derived pointer into the state record when the command byte is below 191. Otherwise it saves the previous table entry, sets a flag and loads a new entry from the table, then writes the stack argument back to the input record.

name: save_and_load_table_entry
description: Saves the current table entry into a state field, sets one flag and clears another, then loads a new table entry indexed by the low six bits of a record byte. It writes the stack argument back into the input record and returns the first argument.

name: reset_channel_load_value
description: Loads a value from a per-channel state table into a global and clears two per-channel state entries for the channel selected by the low bits of the data register. Nothing else is written.

name: reset_channel_and_fill_tables
description: Resets a channel record by loading starting values from a per-period table indexed by the record, clearing its counters and flags and filling a block of eight table entries with a fixed value. If a flag bit is set it reloads saved values from the global table instead, and it finishes by clearing several RAM status bytes.

name: fill_table_and_clear_flags
description: Fills a block of table entries with a fixed value and clears the channel counters and flags, repeating in steps until the index passes zero. A sentinel mismatch triggers a call to another routine, and at the end it clears several RAM status bytes and sets a completion flag.

name: clear_channel_status_and_volume
description: Zeroes the status bytes of several channel blocks that are spaced four bytes apart and writes fifteen, the Amiga volume maximum, to a global volume value. It makes no calls and returns the unchanged data register.

name: sync_and_restore_saved_globals
description: Saves two global words, waits for a shared counter to finish and then for a flag set by another routine. It writes default values into three words of a context block and restores the saved globals before returning.

name: compose_bitplanes_and_start_display
description: Clears a memory block and ORs four bitplane source images together row by row into a combined bitplane buffer. It then builds a 32-entry table of bit masks, clears the background colour register, sets the display control register, points the copper list at the buffer and enables DMA and interrupts.

name: check_cia_timer_flag
description: Checks a flag bit and, when it is set, waits briefly, clears a control bit on one CIA chip and reads the low timer byte of that chip. If the timer byte matches an expected pattern it stores a constant into a global, and it finally sets a context word.

name: select_action_from_state_word
description: Compares a state word with a particular value and calls one of two sets of subroutines depending on the result. When the state word matches it stores a routine reference into a global, and it sets a context word to sixteen before returning.

name: guard_value_limit_then_call
description: Runs a subroutine, then compares a signed 16-bit value read from the base register with the limit one hundred seventy-nine and calls a second subroutine when the value is greater. It then sets a context word to sixteen and returns.

name: update_table_flag_empty
description: Counts down a timer and, once it expires, reloads it and walks a table of sixteen words, masking each word and subtracting a per-entry step from non-zero entries while counting the changes. If no entries changed it stores a sentinel value of one thousand one into a status global.

name: draw_xor_line_after_delay
description: Walks from one point to another on a one-bit bitplane with forty-byte rows, using the signs and magnitudes of the coordinate deltas to step. Pixels are toggled with an exclusive-or only after an initial five-step delay.

name: advance_path_step_and_finish
description: Moves a position by a step taken from a sequence table, decrementing a frame count and advancing through the sequence. When the sequence ends it stores a finished sentinel and clears several status words and RAM bytes.

name: clear_status_and_context_words
description: Zeroes two RAM status bytes and four context words in the record addressed by the base register. It makes no calls and returns immediately afterwards.

name: copy_table_into_record_rows
description: When a request flag is set, copies twenty-eight two-word table entries into rows of a destination buffer spaced forty bytes apart, also copies extra words from fixed table positions, and then clears the flag. It returns nothing.

name: advance_frame_and_compute_address
description: Computes a screen buffer address from a position, moves a frame index through a ten-step cycle and loads two frame values from tables. It then calls four subroutines and stores one thousand one as a completion status.

name: blit_masked_rows_with_shift
description: Combines twenty-eight rows of source and destination data, shifting each source longword by a bit count from the data register and merging it through a mask taken from a table. Source and destination pointers advance forty bytes per row.

name: advance_timed_sequence_entries
description: Runs over seven timer slots, decrementing each countdown. When a countdown expires and its sequence index is not the end marker, it resets the countdown to three, advances the index and calls subroutines.

name: copy_column_with_row_stride
description: Copies a run of values from a source buffer into a destination, advancing forty bytes per entry for the count held in a data register. It copies words when a flag is set and single bytes otherwise.

name: copy_four_bitplane_block
description: Copies an eighteen by eighteen byte block from four source bitplanes into a destination buffer, placing each plane at its own fixed offset. The source bytes are read in row order and no calls are made.

name: scroll_tile_rows_by_zone
description: Scrolls rows of a screen buffer that has forty-byte row stride, choosing one of several copy zones from a row index. In the zones it copies tile bytes between offsets, and in one branch it shifts bit pairs of plane data according to per-entry counters. The listing was truncated, so only its first part was read.

name: run_audio_channel_frame_update
description: Sets pointers, lengths and periods for two audio channels on the first call, then advances a counter and calls subroutines that update the channels in one of three counter ranges. Afterwards it stores one masked bit from a status word and increments the step counter.

name: set_audio_channel_sequence_step
description: Sets pointers, lengths and periods for two audio channels when the step counter is zero, and enables DMA for one channel at a later step. At one specific step it reloads both channels with a fixed sample pointer and length, and it advances the step counter at the end.

name: accumulate_and_store_value
description: Adds a value passed in the data register to a 32-bit accumulator at one location and copies the result to a second location. It makes no calls.

name: initialise_oscillator_from_table
description: Loads a period byte and a step byte from a table entry into two record fields, copies a word between the output and a second field, and clears an accumulator word. It returns nothing.

name: oscillate_offset_on_countdown
description: When the enable byte is set, adds a signed step to an accumulator and writes the sum plus a stored base value to an output word. It counts down a byte, and when the count reaches zero it reloads the count and reverses the step direction.

name: load_step_fields_from_table
description: Copies one byte and one word from a table entry into the record fields that hold the step state. It makes no calls.

name: step_value_and_store_byte
description: When an enable byte and a step word are both nonzero, adds the step word to a 16-bit accumulator and stores its low byte into a record field. Otherwise it returns without changes.

name: square_to_pseudorandom_value
description: Squares a global value offset by a constant, keeps the low half of the product and squares it again, storing the high half of the result into a record field. It makes no calls.

name: describe_undecompiled_routine_body
description: The decompiler timed out, so no pseudo-code exists for this routine. The listed facts show nine instructions, one position-relative address load and two unnamed callers, and nothing more can be said about its behaviour.

name: configure_dma_and_interrupts
description: Writes to the DMA control, interrupt enable and interrupt request registers, with four calls to other routines. No pseudo-code was produced, so the exact sequence of writes is not known.

name: init_entry_table_copper
description: Clears a table of ten five-word entries, marking the first word of each as an empty sentinel, then points the copper list at a buffer and clears the copper jump register. It enables interrupts and DMA afterwards.

name: count_pending_status_events
description: Checks bit four of a global status word and, when it is set, increments an event counter and calls two follow-up routines if the status word is nonzero. It then clears the top bit of the status word and returns the data register unchanged.

name: acknowledge_interrupt_status_bit
description: Tests bit four of a global status word and, when it is set, increments a counter and calls follow-up routines, the interrupt request registers being part of the hardware touched. It then clears the top bit of the status word.

name: step_nibble_fields_after_countdown
description: When a counter byte is zero, moves the three four-bit fields of each of thirty-two words one step toward a target value, recombining them afterwards. Otherwise it only decrements the counter byte.

name: step_nibble_fields_toward_target
description: Decrements a counter byte, then runs the same four-bit field stepping loop over thirty-two words, moving each field one step toward its target and recombining the fields. The loop runs unconditionally on this path.

name: forward_to_jump_vector
description: The decompiler timed out, so the body is unknown. The listed facts show four instructions and one call, which goes through a single absolute jump entry that passes control to another fixed address.

name: unpack_powerpacker_bitstream
description: Checks that a four-byte tag spells PP20, the header of the PowerPacker compression format, and then decodes bit-packed control codes read backwards from the end of the packed data. Literal bytes and back-references are written backwards into the output until the output pointer reaches the start.

name: unpack_powerpacker_with_bounds
description: Performs the same PP20 tag check and backwards bit-packed decoding as its sibling, reading the tag through an address register. It stops when the output pointer reaches a lower bound passed in a second address register.

name: shift_left_insert_low_bit
description: Shifts the 16-bit data register left by one place and fills the vacated bit with the lowest bit of another register. It makes no calls.

name: collect_bits_from_packed_longs
description: Collects a run of bits from packed longwords by taking the lowest bit of the current longword on each step and shifting it into the result. After thirty-two bits it loads the previous longword from the stream pointer.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: Contains only a return instruction, so it does nothing when called. It is a stub with no calls, no hardware access and no data access.

description: Contains only a return instruction, so it does nothing when called. It is a stub with no calls, no hardware access and no data access.

name: read_cia_a_fire_port
description: The decompiler timed out, so the body is unknown. The listed facts show three instructions that touch the CIA A port A register, which carries the joystick and mouse fire button lines and disk status, and three unnamed callers.

name: drive_cia_b_port_calls
description: The decompiler timed out, so the body is unknown. The listed facts show thirty-two instructions that touch the CIA B port B register, five calls to other routines and two unnamed callers.

name: xor_scramble_then_jump_payload
description: Opens libraries through the exec library and then XORs a memory region with a generated shift-register bit stream. It copies a block into place, clears a following block and finally jumps through a table address built during the run. The text references name the OS emulation and DOS libraries.

name: busy_wait_loop_count
description: Counts a data register down to zero in a loop and returns, giving a pure delay with no calls and no hardware access.

name: stub_entry_halts_unimplemented
description: Program entry point that stores a constant into a global and then reaches an unimplemented instruction, so the decompiler stops there. Nothing beyond the store is known from the listing.

name: add_six_and_call_library
description: Adds six to a global value and then makes an indirect call through a fixed offset from the base register, the usual form of an Amiga library call. It returns afterwards.

name: copy_byte_call_library
description: Copies one table byte into a neighbouring location, sets bits in a byte addressed by another register, then calls an Amiga library function at offset minus one hundred thirty-three. The library call is the only external call in the listing.

name: set_global_bits_and_return
description: ORs the low byte of the data register with the mask fifty-six, stores the result in a global and returns it.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Subtracts eight from a word at the address held in an address register, then the decompiler reports bad instruction data and truncates the listing. Only the subtraction is certain, and the rest is bad data.

name: store_value_return_masked
description: Stores the data register value into a global, zeroes two other globals and returns the low byte of the input ORed with twenty-four.

name: store_rotated_control_word
description: Stores a byte-rotated form of the data register into a record field and copies one global value into four consecutive long fields. It then writes a fixed control word with its top bit set to a register offset.

name: call_pair_then_clear_global
description: Calls two subroutines in sequence, then clears a global value twice and returns.

name: store_byte_to_global
description: Stores the low byte of the data register into a global variable and returns.

name: scan_iff_form_body_chunks
description: Walks a chain of FORM blocks, searching each one for a BODY chunk. For each block it stores half of the chunk length and a pointer to the body data into a table, then moves on to the next form.

name: decode_channel_command_stream
description: Runs a decoder over a byte stream of command codes that has an end marker and several code ranges choosing lengths or table entries, updating per-channel state records. The listing is truncated, so only its opening structure is described.

name: decode_channel_command_entry
description: Initialises the state tables for several channels, then runs a command-stream decoder similar to its neighbour. The listing is truncated, so only its opening structure is described.

name: read_table_until_nonnegative
description: Reads bytes from a table selected by a data register index, advancing a counter in the record and wrapping on a sentinel, until it reads a non-negative value. It then copies a table entry into a global pointer and returns.

name: store_offset_and_read_table
description: Stores the data byte plus sixty-four into a record field, then reads table bytes until a non-negative value appears and copies a table entry into a global pointer. A sentinel value restarts the read.

name: copy_table_entry_by_index
description: Copies a longword from a global table, selected by the low byte of the data register scaled by four, into a table slot at an offset held in another register, and also into a global pointer. It makes no calls.

name: advance_channel_sequence_state
description: Advances the playback state of one channel in a command-driven sequence. When the channel's state byte is zero it clears a flag bit, and otherwise it reads command bytes from a stream and branches on code ranges that set lengths and table indexes. The listing is truncated, so only the first part is described.

name: apply_channel_modulation_step
description: Updates a channel's counters and applies a table-driven step to a stored value, using bit flags in the channel record to choose between the increment and decrement paths. The listing is truncated after its first branches.

name: run_channel_command_dispatch
description: Clears the channel state fields when a counter is nonnegative, then reads command bytes from the channel stream and dispatches codes that set loop flags, lengths and effect values. The listing is truncated, so later branches are not described.

name: decrement_channel_counter_step
description: Decrements a channel counter and then calls the shared command decoder, which in this listing is the same routine as its neighbours. Only the counter update is certain, because the rest is truncated.

name: increment_channel_counter_step
description: Increments a channel counter and then calls the shared command decoder, which in this listing is the same routine as its neighbours. The rest of the listing is truncated.

name: clear_flag_and_decrement_counter
description: If a channel flag is set, clears it and decrements the channel counter, then enters a loop that calls the shared update routine and the command decoder. The listing is truncated.

name: reset_channel_state_and_decode
description: Clears several channel state fields, then decodes command bytes from the channel stream and dispatches codes that set loop counts, lengths and effect values. The listing is truncated, so its later branches are not described.

name: dispatch_channel_command_byte
description: Dispatches a command byte from a channel stream: an end marker returns to the caller, a range of codes sets lengths and flags, and the remaining codes store a table-derived value. The listing is truncated, so later branches are not described.

name: decode_next_command_byte
description: Reads the next command byte from a channel stream and dispatches it through the same range tests as its neighbours, setting length, flag and effect fields. The listing is truncated.

name: decode_command_and_set_length
description: Dispatches a command byte from a channel stream, setting a length value for codes in the upper range and passing the rest through the shared branches. The tail of the routine, which stores counters, is truncated.

name: decode_channel_effect_codes
description: Handles the effect codes at the top of the command range, storing a value and setting a flag, then advances the stream pointer and returns through the shared update. The listing is truncated.

name: branch_on_special_command_code
description: Tests a command byte against the special codes in the top range, setting a loop flag, a repeat count or a parameter taken from the next byte, then continues with the shared update. The listing is truncated.

name: handle_special_command_codes
description: Handles the special command codes by setting channel flags and reading their parameters from the stream, then passes control to the shared update. The listing is truncated.

name: read_command_parameter_bytes
description: Reads one or two parameter bytes that follow a special command code, stores them in channel fields and advances the stream pointer before continuing into the shared update. The listing is truncated.

name: read_offset_and_length_parameters
description: Handles command codes that carry a length and an offset parameter, reading the following bytes into channel fields before the shared update. The listing is truncated.

name: update_channel_and_touch_dma
description: Runs the shared channel update and touches the DMA control register, where a write with the top bit set enables DMA channels. The listing is truncated, so the full register sequence is not known.

name: apply_table_driven_step_value
description: Applies a table-driven step to a stored value, using a counter and a sign flag, and writes the result back into the channel record. The listing is truncated after its first branches.

name: apply_table_step_then_decode
description: Applies a table-driven step to a stored value, then decodes the next command byte from the channel stream, following the same structure as its neighbours. The listing is truncated.

name: run_channel_loop_until_end
description: Loops over channel records, decrementing a counter and updating flags, then calls the shared update. An end-of-stream branch writes the value 255 as the end state. The listing is truncated before the loop finishes.

name: step_channel_value_then_decode
description: Applies a table-driven step to a channel value in a loop, then runs the channel update and, when the channel's state byte is zero, decodes the next command bytes. The listing is truncated.

name: subtract_table_step_and_update
description: Subtracts a table-driven step from a stored word in a loop controlled by a channel counter, then runs the channel update. The listing is truncated.

name: add_channel_word_then_update
description: Stores a word from the channel table into the record and runs the channel update that the neighbouring routines share. The listing is truncated.

name: adjust_channel_word_by_step
description: Adds or subtracts a stored step value to a channel word, choosing the direction from a flag, and otherwise reads a table entry indexed by the channel counter. The listing is truncated before the update.

name: copy_indexed_table_word_step
description: Copies a word from a table at an index formed from the channel counter and a data register into the record, increments the counter and runs the channel update. The listing is truncated.

name: apply_step_to_channel_word
description: Applies a signed step to a channel word and stores the result, then runs the channel update. The listing is truncated, so its later branches are not described.

name: add_channel_offset_and_store
description: Adds a 16-bit offset from the data register to a word read from the record and stores the sum back, then writes it into the channel table and runs the channel update. The listing is truncated.

name: update_channel_level_step
description: Computes a shifted value from a channel table entry and compares it with a counter, updating the stored channel level and clearing a status bit when the level reaches zero. It then runs the channel update. The listing is truncated.

name: decrement_channel_level_step
description: Sets a channel status field and subtracts a decrement value from the channel level. When the result is zero or negative it clears the level and sets a bit in a global status byte, otherwise it stores the new level, then runs the channel update. The listing is truncated.

name: clear_channel_level_and_flag
description: Zeroes the channel level byte, sets the bit for the channel in a global status byte and runs the channel update. The listing is truncated.

name: write_audio_channel_pointers_lengths
description: Writes the length and pointer registers of four audio channels from two tables, halving each length and combining each pointer with a twelve-bit offset, after running the channel update. It finishes by storing the value 255 as a status global, an end state.

name: clear_audio_volumes_and_status
description: Zeroes the volume registers of four audio channels and clears one global value and three RAM status bytes. It makes no calls.

name: call_routine_then_clear_globals
description: Calls one subroutine, then clears two global values and returns. The routine is a short wrapper with no other effects.

name: build_active_channel_index_list
description: Scans the eight bits of a global mask and copies the index of each set bit into a list in the record, ending the list with the value 255 and clearing a pending-flag field. It returns the input registers unchanged.

name: divide_table_word_difference
description: Takes the difference between two table words selected by two indexes, swapping the operands so the difference is positive, then performs a twelve-step shift-and-subtract division by a byte value. The rounded quotient is left in a shared word.

name: divide_indexed_word_difference
description: Takes the difference between two table words selected by two data register indexes, then performs a twelve-step shift-and-subtract division by a byte value, leaving the rounded quotient in a shared word.

name: load_channel_parameters_from_table
description: Copies six parameter bytes for a channel from the table row chosen by the channel's index byte. When a further table byte is nonzero it also sets two state fields and calls the shared update.

name: set_audio_pointer_length
description: Loads channel state bytes from a table row, selects a sample pointer and a length by index, and writes them to the audio channel pointer and length registers. The listing stores to the same location twice, so only the second store takes effect.

name: copy_table_word_to_slot
description: Reads a word from a global table at an index derived from a record byte and stores it into a global slot, with two identical stores. It makes no calls.

name: restore_audio_period_and_volumes
description: Writes saved period values to the period registers of four audio channels, then computes a control word from saved state and writes volume values to the four volume registers. The facts also list the DMA control register among those touched.

name: run_init_and_read_sequence
description: Calls, in order, routines that allocate memory, initialise state, start the sequence, seek to track zero, read, clear, check a signature and free memory, then returns the status byte. The routine has no other logic of its own.

name: save_and_reset_interrupt_registers
description: Saves the current interrupt enable, interrupt request and DMA control values into globals, then writes masks that disable the interrupt master enable, clear one pending request and set the DMA master enable. It finishes by setting bits in a global status byte.

name: clear_status_bits_then_wait
description: Clears the top bit of a global status byte and runs a countdown of one hundred steps, clearing one bit of the same byte on each step. It then calls the wait routine, and the CIA B port register is among those touched.

name: delay_then_wait_status_bit
description: Runs a countdown of three thousand steps, then spins while bit five of a global status byte is set. It touches the CIA A port register, which holds the fire button and disk status lines.

name: wait_while_status_bit_set
description: While bit four of a global status byte is set, sets the two low bits of that byte and calls the wait routine, returning once the bit has cleared. The CIA A port register is among the registers touched.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: Contains only a return instruction, so it does nothing when called.

name: wait_out_status_bit_sequence
description: Calls the seek routine while bit four of a global status byte is set, then runs a loop whose condition is false on entry, so the loop body never runs. The CIA A port register is among the registers touched.

name: stub_loop_never_executes
description: Contains a counting loop whose condition is false on entry, so its body never runs and the routine returns at once.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: Contains only a return instruction, so it does nothing when called.

name: start_dma_poll_interrupt
description: Clears a bit in a global status byte, points a DMA location at a buffer and enables DMA through the DMA control register, then calls the wait routine. It writes a fixed control value to a second register and polls the interrupt request bits for up to two hundred thousand iterations, acknowledging the request when it is set.

name: disable_dma_channel_and_clear
description: Writes zero to a register at offset thirty-six of the record and writes the value sixteen to the DMA control register. Without the top bit set, that write disables the channel that bit four selects, and the routine makes no calls.

name: wait_for_flag_bit
description: Spins until bit four of a global status byte becomes set, then returns. The facts also list the CIA B interrupt control register as touched.

name: restore_saved_interrupt_dma
description: Clears bit three of a global status byte and sets its top bit, then writes the saved interrupt enable, interrupt request, DMA and disk and audio control values back to their registers with the top bit set, which enables those bits.

name: search_sync_pattern_bitwise
description: Scans a buffer bit by bit for a sixteen-bit sync pattern, then scans on for a second match and compares the count of bits passed with a fixed threshold. It writes zero or one into a status byte according to that comparison.

name: check_sync_pattern_distance
description: Scans forward word by word for the sixteen-bit sync pattern, checking each bit position and counting the words passed. When the pattern is found it writes zero or one into a status byte according to a fixed threshold comparison.

name: set_status_from_threshold
description: Compares a value in a data register with a fixed threshold of six thousand seven hundred and writes zero to the status byte when the value is at or above it, otherwise one.

name: set_status_to_one
description: Writes one to the status byte and returns. It makes no other calls.

name: call_pair_then_clear_global
description: Calls two subroutines and then clears a global value twice before returning. It has no other effects.

name: call_pair_then_clear_global
description: Calls two subroutines and then clears a global value twice before returning. It has no other effects.

name: call_pair_then_clear_global
description: Calls two subroutines and then clears a global value twice before returning. It has no other effects.

name: copy_longwords_in_endless_loop
description: Loops without an exit, copying one longword per pass from a source pointer into a destination offset from another register, with three calls to a shared routine on each pass. Nothing in the listing ends the loop.

name: copy_longword_and_call_pair
description: Loops without an exit: copies one longword from a source pointer to a destination and to a global, calls a shared routine twice and then advances the source pointer.

name: copy_longword_and_call_pair
description: Loops without an exit: copies one longword from a source pointer to a destination and to a global, calls a shared routine twice and then advances the source pointer.

name: copy_longword_and_call_pair
description: Loops without an exit: copies one longword from a source pointer to a destination and to a global, calls a shared routine twice and then advances the source pointer.

name: run_main_loop_after_open
description: Calls a library-opening routine and, if that fails, stays in an empty infinite loop. Otherwise it makes setup calls, clears a status byte and runs a main loop of state-checking routines until a completion flag is set, then jumps to a computed routine.

name: open_graphics_library_or_fail
description: Calls the library-open routine with the graphics library name referenced in the text, stores a non-zero base address in a global and returns it. If the open fails it returns the value one hundred.

name: lay_out_buffers_clear_block
description: Calls the exec and graphics library routines listed in the facts for forbidding multitasking, taking and releasing the blitter and waiting for a blit. It then lays out buffer pointers at fixed offsets from a base address and zeroes a block of one thousand three hundred and sixty bytes.

name: restore_copper_and_close_libraries
description: Calls library routines that the facts identify as closing libraries, removing an interrupt server and releasing the blitter. Between the calls it waits for a fixed countdown of fifty thousand steps and writes the copper list pointer register from a library field.

name: decode_iff_ilbm_chunks
description: Reads IFF picture chunks: a header chunk, a colour map whose RGB triplets are packed into four-bit-per-channel colour words, and a body chunk decompressed with PackBits-style run decoding into rows. It closes the file through a DOS call when done.

name: mask_word_and_call_routine
description: ANDs a word addressed by a register with a fixed mask that keeps only bits eight and ten, then calls a shared routine and returns.

name: mask_word_and_call_routine
description: ANDs a word addressed by a register with a fixed mask that keeps only bits eight and ten, then calls a shared routine and returns.

name: mask_word_and_call_routine
description: ANDs a word addressed by a register with a fixed mask that keeps only bits eight and ten, then calls a shared routine and returns.

name: mask_word_and_call_routine
description: ANDs a word addressed by a register with a fixed mask that keeps only bits eight and ten, then calls a shared routine and returns.

name: forward_to_single_routine
description: Makes one call to a shared routine and returns, with no other effect.

name: call_shared_routine_once
description: Calls one shared routine and returns. The facts also list a small instruction that merges a constant into a register before the call.

name: fill_row_table_from_calls
description: Computes a row offset of forty bytes times a stored index, then fills a table with the values returned by a routine, one entry per pass, for a count held in memory plus one.

name: decode_iff_chunks_until_done
description: Repeatedly reads IFF-style chunks: a header, a colour map packing RGB triplets into four-bit-per-channel colour words, and a body decompressed with PackBits-style run decoding into rows of forty bytes. It loops until a completion flag is set and then calls a closing routine.

name: copy_buffered_bytes_refilling
description: Copies bytes one at a time from a file buffer into the destination, and when the buffer position reaches one thousand it calls the library read routine and resets the position. It returns the last position used.

name: open_file_and_reset_buffer
description: Calls the DOS open routine, then calls the DOS read routine, and resets the buffer position to zero. It returns the result of the open call.

name: parse_decimal_digits_from_stream
description: Reads bytes from a stream and accumulates decimal digits into a number with a multiply-by-ten step, stopping at the first non-digit. It records whether any digit was read.

name: fill_buffer_words_then_close
description: Computes a word count from two stored values, fills a buffer one word per pass with a value taken from a global, and closes a file through the DOS close routine.

name: store_call_result_at_pointer
description: Makes two calls to shared routines, makes a third call and stores its returned value through a pointer held in a global. It returns afterwards.

name: store_call_result_at_pointer
description: Makes two calls to shared routines, makes a third call and stores its returned value through a pointer held in a global. It returns afterwards.

name: allocate_memory_and_record_pointer
description: Stores an input longword in a table slot selected by a counter, calls the exec memory allocation routine, and when it returns a non-zero pointer stores that pointer in the next slot and advances the counter by eight. On failure it calls another routine and returns zero.

name: stub_or_mask_likely_data
description: Returns its input ORed with the mask two hundred fifty-four. The listed instruction count is far larger than this single operation, so the bytes are probably data that decodes as code.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: Contains only a return instruction, so it does nothing when called.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: Contains only a return instruction, so it does nothing when called.

name: free_memory_block_from_table
description: If a table counter is nonzero, steps it back by eight and calls the exec memory-free routine to release the most recent allocation. Otherwise it returns without action.

name: stub_immediate_return
description: Contains only a return instruction, so it does nothing when called.

name: load_graphics_and_sound_assets
description: Opens and reads a series of graphics and sound asset files whose paths appear in the text, using the DOS open and read calls and copying the data into buffers through a loader routine. The referenced paths name picture and sound effect files.

name: update_numbered_asset_load
description: Forbids multitasking through the exec library, builds a numbered asset name by adding the ASCII digit zero to a counter, and when it differs from the stored value copies a block of words to a fixed buffer and reloads the asset. It permits multitasking again before returning.

name: call_routine_until_negative_entry
description: Repeatedly calls a shared routine and advances over a byte table until it reaches an entry whose top bit is set, which marks the end of the table.

name: call_routine_until_end_marker
description: Walks a byte list, calling a shared routine for each entry, until it reaches an entry equal to minus one.

name: poll_routine_until_one
description: Calls a shared routine repeatedly until it returns the value one, then returns zero.

name: store_word_for_set_bits
description: Examines the low two bits of the byte in the data register and, for each bit that is set, stores a word from another register into a table slot selected by that bit position.

name: forward_to_single_routine
description: Makes one call to a shared routine and returns, with no other effect.

name: clear_large_buffer_bytes
description: Writes zero to sixteen thousand consecutive bytes starting at a buffer pointer. It makes no calls.

name: read_keyboard_serial_code
description: Fills an eight-byte area with dot characters, polls the keyboard serial register through several calls until a count is reached, then checks the stored bytes against a fixed four-byte pattern and a key-code range. A match sets a flag and stores a key index.

name: call_three_routines_in_order
description: Calls three shared routines in order and returns, with no other effect.

name: call_three_routines_in_order
description: Calls three shared routines in order and returns, with no other effect.

name: translate_key_code_to_character
description: Converts a keyboard code into a character by inverting and halving it to index a table. One special code returns one, another stores a period, and a third calls a shared routine. The result is stored in a buffer and a state byte is updated.

name: translate_key_code_to_character
description: Converts a keyboard code into a character by inverting and halving it to index a table. One special code returns one, another stores a period, and a third calls a shared routine. The result is stored in a buffer and a state byte is updated.

name: step_back_store_period
description: If a state byte is not at its limit, decrements it, stores a fixed code of twenty-six into a buffer, calls a shared routine and writes a period character into a table slot indexed by the state byte.

name: copy_two_table_rows
description: Stores the code thirty-four into a global and calls a shared routine, then copies eight bytes from a fixed table into a buffer. It then does the same with the code thirty-five and returns.

name: set_display_registers_and_copper
description: Writes fixed values to the display control, bitplane control, colour, display window and fetch registers, enables DMA through the DMA control register and points the copper list at a buffer. It returns a status word read from a register. The facts also list the blitter mask registers among those touched.

name: copy_table_sentinel_call
description: Copies words from a table into a buffer until it copies the sentinel value of minus two, then calls four shared routines and returns.

name: copy_table_blocks_into_buffer
description: Copies a run of eight words, then a run of sixteen words, then a two-by-four block of words from a table into a buffer at fixed strides. It makes no calls.

name: fill_mask_arrays_copy_table
description: Sets two byte arrays to the value 255 across two hundred passes, then copies seventy-four bytes from a table into both arrays at an offset.

name: build_display_list_rows
description: Writes a repeating block of ten words for each step of a counter into a display list buffer, using constant words and offsets computed from two byte tables and buffer bases. It calls a shared routine for each computed offset.

name: write_list_header_copy_table
description: Writes a header word and an override word into a list buffer, copies words from a global table until the sentinel minus two, then writes two trailing words from a fixed address. It makes no calls.
